name: John Allen Kurrle Jr.

attribution.legal_posture: DOJ reports that the court accepted Kurrle’s guilty plea to conspiracy to commit wire fraud on October 28, 2026. Sentencing was scheduled for January 28, 2027; the release establishes no imposed sentence. The accepted plea is distinct from DOJ’s account of scheme conduct and its general North Korean IT-worker background.

identity_boundary: The defendant John Allen Kurrle Jr. in E.D. Va. case 1:26-cr-198, as identified by DOJ. No identity link to another person or overseas worker is inferred.
caveats: One DOJ source family supports this record.
The guilty plea, reported conduct and scheduled sentencing are distinct evidential and legal postures.

sources.support: Reports the named defendant’s accepted guilty plea, case number, alleged scheme methods, job offers and separately scheduled sentencing.

value.name: John Allen Kurrle Jr.
value.court: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia

value.posture: accepted guilty plea reported by DOJ

sources.quote: pled guilty today to conspiracy to commit wire fraud relating to a scheme involving fraudulent applications for remote employment using borrowed U.S. identities.
made the announcement after U.S. District Judge Michael S. Nachmanoff accepted the plea.
Kurrle is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 28, 2027

notes: This is a scheduled event, not an imposed sentence or evidence that sentencing has occurred.

value.reported_conduct: allowed foreign individuals to use his identity and fraudulently use a third person’s identity for remote-employment applications
value.source_posture: DOJ account attributed to court documents

sources.quote: According to court documents from June to August 2025

During that time, Kurrle participated in a scheme to defraud U.S. companies, including U.S. government contractors, in which he allowed foreign individuals to use his identity to apply for remote work positions and to fraudulently use the identity of a third person to apply for remote positions.

notes: The general North Korean IT-worker background in the release does not identify an individual overseas worker or establish an identity link to any other catalog subject.

value.reported_conduct: received employer-issued laptops and enabled remote access from outside the United States

sources.quote: Kurrle received laptops shipped by victim companies
enabled remote access from outside the United States.

value.scope: applications using Kurrle’s identity or a stolen identity

sources.quote: The applications using Kurrle’s identity or a stolen identity induced nine job offers from U.S. companies.
